entries.notes: KERNEL: audit_netlink_ok() (kernel/audit.c, 6.12) returns ECONNREFUSED for any caller outside the initial user namespace and EPERM for AUDIT_GET/SET/LIST_RULES/ADD_RULE/DEL_RULE outside the initial PID namespace or without CAP_AUDIT_CONTROL. The suite reason and the candidate help (loadables/audit.c:1104-1124) name CAP_AUDIT_READ/CAP_AUDIT_WRITE, which are not the gating capabilities for these message types. The legacy runner (new user+PID ns, no caps) and all modern drivers (uid 2000) can therefore only observe the refusal paths. Candidate: ba_cmd_run loadables/audit.c:912-1001. Event reception is unicast to the registered pid; run is not bounded if -c and -t are both 0, so fixtures must pass a bound.

entries.notes: Semantic difference to check: bashmount --remount passes MS_REMOUNT|flags without MS_BIND (bashmount.c:680-686), which changes super-block flags. util-linux `mount -o remount,ro` on a bind mount uses MS_REMOUNT|MS_BIND in libmount, which changes the per-mount flag only. A remount of a bind target may therefore diverge (unexecuted prediction).

original.purpose: Exercise bind, recursive bind, and remount behavior including read-only follow-up remount handling.

requirements.behavior: -B SRC DST bind-mounts a relative directory: DST shows SRC's contents, and mountinfo shows the same superblock with an FSROOT of the source subtree.

evidence.assertion: -B src dst (relative) shows src contents in dst; mountinfo root is /src on the base tmpfs device number, equal to a util-linux --bind control

requirements.behavior: -R recursively binds, including a submount nested under SRC. A plain -B must not carry that submount.

evidence.assertion: -R carries the nested tmpfs submount (mountpoint present, inner file visible) like util-linux --rbind, while plain -B shows no submount and an empty directory

requirements.behavior: -B -o ro issues the bind and then a MS_BIND|MS_REMOUNT|MS_RDONLY follow-up. The resulting bind is read-only (writes fail with EROFS) while the source stays writable.

evidence.assertion: -B -o ro: writes through the bind fail while the source stays writable; per-mount ro without superblock ro, equal to util-linux bind then remount,bind,ro

requirements.behavior: --remount -o ro DST (and -o rw) changes an existing mount's flags; super-block versus per-mount effects are compared with util-linux `mount -o remount,ro`.

evidence.assertion: --remount -o ro then -o rw: direct and via-bind writes fail then succeed (superblock-wide for tmpfs), and mountinfo mount/super options equal a raw MS_REMOUNT control (util-linux remount fails here with an invalid uid option for tmpfs)

requirements.behavior: Argument errors: -B/-R with the wrong operand count, --remount without DST, and conflicting verbs return the documented usage status.

evidence.assertion: -B/-R with one or three operands, --remount with none or two, and bind+rbind, remount+bind and remount+list conflicts all return status 2 with the documented diagnostic

entries.notes: Source: loadables/bashmount.c:80-131 (option table and data forwarding) and :360-386 (bm_do_mount; the fs-type probe is skipped for bind/remount). Without -t, the candidate probes every type in /proc/filesystems (bm_probe_types, :338). util-linux uses libmount/blkid instead, so an untyped mount may diverge. Locked-flag semantics differ when the namespace is created inside a user namespace: remounting away MNT_LOCK_* flags inherited from the parent fails with EPERM. Use a fresh tmpfs created inside the namespace so no flags are locked.

original.purpose: Exercise plain typed mounts, option flag mapping, and filesystem-specific data forwarding.
original.reason: Requires a disposable VM with a dedicated mount namespace and disposable tmpfs target, or a reviewed mount(2) mock that records source, target, type, flags, and data. requirements.behavior: A plain typed mount of a tmpfs onto a relative directory succeeds; afterwards the target is a mountpoint of fstype tmpfs, and files written into it live on the new filesystem.

evidence.assertion: bashmount -t tmpfs tmpfs one succeeds (rc 0); independent mountinfo parse shows one as a mountpoint with fstype tmpfs equal to the util-linux control; st_dev differs from the parent, the written file reads back live and vanishes after unmount while the directory remains

requirements.behavior: Known option names map to MS_* flags: -o ro,nosuid,nodev,noexec,noatime yields the matching per-mount options in mountinfo, and rw/suid/dev/exec clear the opposite bits.

evidence.assertion: -o ro,nosuid,nodev,noexec,noatime yields per-mount options noatime,nodev,noexec,nosuid,ro identical to util-linux; a later --remount -o rw,suid,dev,exec clears ro/nosuid/noexec/nodev (noatime retained per mount(2)) and equals a raw MS_REMOUNT control

evidence.assertion: -o size=64k,ro,nosuid: tmpfs super options contain size=64k and ro, mount options contain ro,nosuid, size= is not a mount flag, and both option strings equal the util-linux mount result

requirements.behavior: Failure status and diagnostic for a rejected mount: a missing target, an unknown fstype without probing, and an invalid data token such as size=bogus, compared with util-linux mount status classes.

evidence.assertion: missing target, unknown fstype (no probing) and size=bogus fail with status 1 and the kernel errno text matching a raw mount(2) call (ENOENT, ENODEV, EINVAL) and util-linux failure class 32; no mount is created; -t/-o without value, conflicting verbs and one operand return status 2 with the documented message

requirements.behavior: No host mount changes: every mount is confined to the per-side namespace and is gone after the side ends.

evidence.assertion: plain mount, bind, remount and unmount inside the private mapped namespace leave the outer mountinfo byte-identical, with no fixture mountpoint and an empty fixture directory afterwards

entries.notes: Source: loadables/bashmount.c:389-395 (bm_do_umount) and :547-556 (-l means MNT_DETACH only after -u; otherwise it lists; -f is rejected without -u). The parse-only paths (-f without -u returns EX_USAGE) are reachable unprivileged and are not yet executed.

original.purpose: Exercise ordinary, lazy, and force unmount flag mapping and observable cleanup.
original.reason: Requires a disposable VM with disposable private-namespace mounts, or a reviewed umount2(2) mock that records flags. Verify normal, -l/MNT_DETACH, and -f/MNT_FORCE calls and cleanup/error behavior; no unmount operation is run in this suite.

requirements.behavior: -u DST performs an ordinary unmount: the mount disappears from mountinfo and the DST directory remains.

evidence.assertion: -u a removes the mount from mountinfo like util-linux umount, the directory remains and the masked file is gone

requirements.behavior: -u -l DST requests MNT_DETACH. With an open descriptor inside DST (exec 3<dst/file) a normal unmount fails with EBUSY, while -l succeeds, detaches DST from mountinfo, and leaves fd 3 readable.

evidence.assertion: with fd 3 open in the mount, -u fails status 1 EBUSY text (raw umount2 EBUSY, still mounted); -u -l succeeds, removes the mountinfo entry and fd 3 still reads its content

requirements.behavior: -u -f DST requests MNT_FORCE, and the status and cleanup are compared with `umount -f`.

evidence.assertion: seccomp-notify records umount2 flags 1 for -f, 2 for -l, 0 for plain and 3 for -l -f; -f succeeds like util-linux umount -f (flags 1, rc 0) in the mapped namespace and the mounts are gone

requirements.behavior: Error behavior: unmounting a non-mountpoint (EINVAL), a missing path (ENOENT), and a busy mount without -l (EBUSY), with nonzero status and diagnostics compared with util-linux umount status classes.

evidence.assertion: non-mountpoint EINVAL, missing path ENOENT and busy mount EBUSY give status 1 with the matching errno text (raw umount2 oracle) and util-linux failure class 32; the busy mount stays; -u without operand and -f without -u return status 2

requirements.behavior: Observable cleanup: after each side, no fixture mount remains in the namespace.

evidence.assertion: after mount/bind/remount/umount in the side namespace the outer namespace has no fixture mount and byte-identical mountinfo

original.purpose: Cover --partx-kernel BLKPG add/delete/update and post-write partition reread behavior.
original.reason: Requires a disposable Linux VM with an isolated throwaway block device or a reviewed ioctl mock that records BLKPG and BLKRRPART requests; the current environment must not issue kernel partition-table ioctls.

requirements.behavior: --partx-kernel add DEV [MIN MAX] issues BLKPG_ADD_PARTITION for each table entry in range so the kernel partition set (/sys/block/loopN/loopNpM start/size) matches the on-disk MBR/GPT, like util-linux partx --add.

evidence.assertion: Range adds on a loop device make sysfs start/size equal the DOS table written by sfdisk (p2, then p3, then p1).

requirements.behavior: --partx-kernel delete and update remove/resize kernel partitions in range; update requires geometry; MIN>MAX and out-of-range bounds are rejected.

evidence.assertion: delete of one partition, update to a rewritten table size, ENXIO for an absent kernel partition, MIN>MAX and over-range bound rejected.
delete MIN MAX over 1..3 then add all again.

requirements.behavior: Non-root refusal: as uid != 0 the command fails with 'BLKPG mutation requires uid 0' before opening the device (fdisk.c:2969-2972); a regular-file image as root fails with 'is not a block device'.

evidence.assertion: Bad OP, non-numeric/negative/over-range bounds, MIN>MAX and wrong operand counts fail with the documented diagnostics (status 1, usage 2), and uid 2000 gets "BLKPG mutation requires uid 0" for add/delete/update.
As root, --partx-kernel add/delete/update on a regular-file image fail with "is not a block device" status 1; together with the non-root refusal case this covers both halves.

requirements.behavior: Post-write partition reread: after a table write on a block device the candidate issues BLKRRPART (fdisk.c:2849) and the kernel partition set reflects the new table; warnings for EBUSY are printed.

evidence.assertion: --create-mbr on a partscan loop device rereads the table (kernel set follows, also when shrinking); mounted partition gives a BLKRRPART EBUSY warning with the table still written; clean after umount.

The GPU start succeeds and the saved two inline chunks reconstruct the 4096-byte canvas. Queue drainage and renewed polling support the inference of consumption; reads were not syscall-traced.

This does not replace the existing rejection and fallback companions.

original.reason: Requires reviewed stat/clock/ttyname mocks or a disposable PTY setup with private synthetic session records. Current fixtures exercise unknown-terminal markers and the no-matching-terminal case only; no live terminal or session database is inspected.

requirements.behavior: -T/-w message status '+' or '-' from the terminal's group-write bit.

evidence.assertion: who -T over real ptys owned by the side (devpts gid 5): mode 0620 prints '+', 0600 '-', /dev/null '+', missing pts/999 '?', identical to GNU who 9.7. who -w (GNU alias of -T) is rejected by the candidate ('invalid option: -w', status 1). Parity FAIL.

requirements.behavior: -u idle durations computed from the terminal's access time ('.' when active, HH:MM, 'old').

evidence.assertion: who -u/-Tu/-a: access time 10 s ago prints '  .', 3725 s '01:02', 90000 s ' old' and a missing line '  ?', identical to GNU. Differences: a future access time prints '  .' (GNU ' old'), and an access time older than a preceding BOOT_TIME record prints '00:33' (GNU ' old', which compares against the boot record). Parity FAIL.

requirements.behavior: -m positive match: only the record for the current terminal (ttyname(stdin)).

evidence.assertion: With stdin redirected from a given pty (in a subshell), who -m, -mT, -mu and -mH select only that terminal's records, identical to GNU; without a terminal on stdin -m prints nothing on both. who -q -m filters to the terminal (u3, users=1) where GNU ignores -m under -q (all five names). Parity FAIL.

original.purpose: Qualify -a byte changes, including multiple signatures and preservation of unrelated fixture data.
original.reason: Requires a disposable VM or reviewed private-image mock that confines all writes to throwaway regular-file images, plus independently encoded signature vectors and an independent util-linux/reference-byte oracle. Verify -a clears only specified magic bytes, preserves neighboring data, and compare repeated/no-match behavior; separately verify -n preserves the image. The destructive operation is not run here.

requirements.behavior: -a on a regular image erases exactly the magic bytes of every detected signature (e.g. ext 0x438 2 bytes and swap page-10 10 bytes in one image) and leaves every other byte unchanged.

evidence.assertion: five signatures in one image and two pairs in two others: only the magic ranges become zero

requirements.behavior: Repeated -a on an already wiped image finds nothing and is silent; -a on a file with no signature is silent, unchanged and successful.

evidence.assertion: repeat -a and listing silent; signature-free file untouched; missing operand between images -> status 1, both processed; read-only -a EACCES
repeat -a silent on both sides

requirements.behavior: -n (and -a -n) lists what would be erased and preserves the image.

evidence.assertion: contract: 'wipefs', 'wipefs -n', 'wipefs --no-act' on an XFSB-prefixed file print '0x0\txfs\timage' three times and the file content is unchanged
contract: 'wipefs -n' lists offsets 0x0 xfs and 0x438 ext; python asserts every image byte unchanged
-a -n, -n -a, --all --no-act, -n list and change nothing; -a -n works on a read-only image

requirements.behavior: Erasure on filesystems created by independent tools (mkfs.ext2, mkfs.fat, mkswap) compared with util-linux wipefs -a byte effects (byte parity of the image; stdout formats differ by design).

evidence.assertion: mkfs.ext2 and mkswap images: same changed byte ranges as util-linux wipefs -a (0x438-0x439, 0xff6-0xfff); zero image untouched

requirements.behavior: -a on a raw block device erases signatures through the device node.

evidence.assertion: -a on a 4 MiB loop device with an ext4 signature erases it through the device node on both sides: a following listing is empty, blkid -p exits 2 and a repeated -a is silent. Listing and erase report formats differ (util-linux table and 'bytes were erased' line versus the candidate's offset/type/device line). Parity FAIL.

original.purpose: Qualify real terminal/session banner, EOF marker and partial-write behavior.
original.reason: Requires a future disposable VM with a private PTY/session driver, a fixed clock/user/host mock and reviewed stat/open/write fault injection. No real terminal recipient or host session may be used. Private regular-file byte checks do not qualify PTY behavior.

requirements.behavior:
Writing to a real PTY recipient delivers the banner '
\a\a\aMessage from USER@HOST on SRCTTY at HH:MM ...
', the message with careful escaping, and a trailing 'EOF
'.

evidence.assertion: raw PTY bytes: CRLF + three BEL + 'Message from u@h on pts/N at HH:MM ...', escaped body 'hi a^[[31mb\351', 'EOF'

requirements.behavior: With messages disabled on the recipient terminal (mode without S_IWGRP|S_IWOTH), write refuses with a diagnostic and delivers nothing.

evidence.assertion: forced mode gate on a private regular-file receiver
after chmod 600 on the real terminal: rc 1, '<tty> has messages disabled', output_lacks 'refused@h'

requirements.behavior: Session semantics: stdin message mode (write TTY, message read until EOF) on a terminal, with the EOF marker emitted at end of input.

evidence.assertion: stdin mode: two typed lines and ^D delivered after the banner as 'line one\r\nline two\r\n' then 'EOF'; rc 0

requirements.behavior: Write faults: an ENOSPC write error (/dev/full as the target) reports an error and nonzero status.

evidence.assertion: /dev/full: banner and (BASHWALL_NOBANNER=1) body writes fail with 'No space left on device', rc 1

requirements.behavior: Partial (short) write handling.

evidence.assertion: Reached on both builds. Real owned PTY sees abc after a first write of 8 requested bytes returned 3; candidate exits 1 without a remainder attempt. Native control retries the remaining 5 and delivers abcdef CRLF with status 0. Original scenario: Positive short write to an actual owned PTY recipient: deliver first3 of8 body bytes before returning3, compare remainder retry and complete bytes/status with native independent write-all control.

requirements.behavior: Parity with util-linux write's user/utmp-based recipient selection.

evidence.assertion: write u1 with a one-record utmp naming u1 on the fixture PTY: the independent model expects the banner, text and EOF on the recipient terminal and status 0; the candidate treats the argument as a device path and fails (FAIL). Debian 13 ships no write command, so the oracle is the write(1) man-page model.

original.purpose: Qualify the documented read retry path when an attribute grows between the size probe and data read.
original.reason: Requires a deterministic syscall interposer or mock that can force ERANGE and control successive getxattr sizes. Do not substitute an uncontrolled concurrent writer race; run this later with a dedicated disposable VM/mock fixture.

requirements.behavior: After a successful size probe, an ERANGE on the data read triggers a re-probe and a larger buffer, and the value is returned intact.

evidence.assertion: For a real 3-byte initial attribute, pause its data read, independently grow it to 9 bytes, continue the real syscall and require exact probe/read sizes 0,3,0,9 and exact returned bytes. A ctypes control confirms the first real read returns ERANGE.

requirements.behavior: Repeated ERANGE stops after 8 rounds with 'ERANGE retry limit exceeded' and nonzero status.

evidence.assertion: Inject ERANGE on all nonzero-length reads and require eight reads with sizes 3,6,12,24,48,96,192,384, nine zero-size probes, status 1 and the retry-limit diagnostic.

requirements.behavior: The same retry path for fgetxattr (-F FD) and lgetxattr (-L).

evidence.assertion: Repeat both growth and exhaustion for syscall fgetxattr using -F on an open fd and lgetxattr using -L on a regular file, in addition to getxattr.

requirements.behavior: A real concurrent growth of the value between probe and read.

evidence.assertion: The unfiltered supervisor performs and verifies an actual 3-to-9-byte user xattr replacement after the successful probe and before the continued data syscall; the ctypes positive control verifies kernel ERANGE and exact grown output.

original.purpose: Exercise byte-exact encoding and decoding across deterministic interrupted reads, short writes and zero writes.
original.reason: Requires a reviewed FD/syscall mock in a future disposable VM to inject EINTR and partial/zero writes deterministically. Ordinary closed-descriptor write failure is covered separately in the private namespace fixture; injected faults are not claimed as passes.

requirements.behavior: Interrupted reads (EINTR) during decode and encode are retried; output bytes are exact.

evidence.assertion: Injected EINTR twice on stdin read(2) is retried for decode and encode in all seven codecs; real trapped-signal EINTR on FIFO reads for gzip decode and encode; output exact.

requirements.behavior: Partial writes are continued until all bytes are written.

evidence.assertion: Injected EINTR then synthetic short count 1000 on stdout write(2) is continued from that offset for all seven codecs; real trapped-signal short writes to a full FIFO for gzip and xz decode give exact output.

requirements.behavior: A zero-byte write is treated as an error, not looped forever.

evidence.assertion: write(2) answered 0: gzip/zlib/deflate report an error after one call (status 1, diagnostic); FAIL: xz, lzma, zstd and bzip2 retry all 200 zero returns and finish with status 0 and no diagnostic (their write loops only check w < 0).

requirements.behavior: A short write followed by an error is reported, and later invocations work.

evidence.assertion: RLIMIT_FSIZE 1 KiB with SIGXFSZ ignored: every codec reports "File too large" with status 1, keeps exactly the first 1024 bytes, and the next invocation after restoring the limit succeeds. PASS lines.

original.purpose: Check the documented decoder window ceiling using a small frame that advertises a window above 128 MiB.
original.reason: Run only in a future disposable VM with at least 512 MiB available memory and an independently generated, size-bounded frame advertising a 256 MiB window. This suite limits runtime fixtures to small resource use, so this operation is DEFERRED and is not counted as passed.

requirements.behavior: A frame whose window descriptor advertises 256 MiB (windowLog 28) is rejected at the documented 128 MiB ceiling (ZS_WINDOW_LOG_MAX 27) with status 1 and no output.

evidence.assertion: parity with zstd 1.5 zstdcat: status, stdout bytes, diagnostic presence

requirements.behavior: The fixture is valid: reference zstd decodes it when its memory limit is raised.

evidence.assertion: parity control frame; setup proves the 256 MiB frame with zstd --memory=256MB

Its own setup_script asserts the exact 256 MiB frame decodes to hello under /usr/bin/zstd --memory=256MB before the rejection comparison; both setups complete successfully. This is a direct valid r2 mapping in addition to the current 128 MiB control.
